clue.text: Look of e.g. Telegraph Puzzles feature

blocks.note: Telegraph Puzzles is an example of a phone app
an ear is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A puzzle fan admires the appearance of an item in the Telegraph's puzzle app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' is the verb here, as in 'seem', not the noun it appears to be next to 'feature'.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to seem or give that impression, which is one sense of the verb.

clue.text: Opening of Pinot wine is an option for a writer

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of Pinot
rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A wine lover considers whether a glass of Pinot might suit a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer chooses between prose and verse, so ordinary non-poetic writing is one of their options.

clue.text: Band of the Eighties period – Yes

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
'sure' is an informal way of saying yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a group belonged to the 1980s and gets the answer yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes was also a real band, a 1970s prog-rock group, which helps the musical surface along.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasure is a British synth-pop duo who had their run of hit singles in the 1980s.

clue.text: Roof components free, say, put up by Europeans

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means its letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to rid is to free
e.g. means 'for example', as does 'say'
Poles are people from Poland

explanation.surface: Builders from Europe put up parts of a roof without charging for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridgepoles are the horizontal beams along the top of a roof or tent, so they are parts of a roof.

clue.text: Snack food from shop Sir Charles brought back

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows
bringing something back sends it the way it came, so the hidden letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of shop, all of Sir and the start of Charles

explanation.surface: A knight named Charles returns from the shop with a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp is a thin fried potato slice, the British name for what Americans call a potato chip.

clue.text: Lolly remains cold on top

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: An ice lolly's leftovers are still cold at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'cold on top' puts C above the other piece. Lolly is British slang for money, not the ice lolly the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolly is informal British slang for money, so it means the same as cash.

clue.text: Would-be high-flyer, one given e.g. Mini and Cross Atlantic?

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the Mini is a famous small car
from Britain, the United States lies across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: Someone who dreams of flying high is given a small car and a transatlantic trip.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus tried to fly on wax wings, rose too near the sun and fell, an aspiring high-flyer.

clue.text: Most prudish cleric admits biases occasionally

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so every other letter is kept
to admit is to let in, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: a priest is a cleric
second, fourth and sixth letters of biases

explanation.surface: A churchman who is very strait-laced lets slip his prejudices now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Prissy means fussily prim and proper, so its superlative is the most prudish.

clue.text: The scene of a cracking victory over Germany?

definitions.text: The scene of a cracking victory over Germany?

blocks.clueFragment: The scene of a cracking victory over Germany?
blocks.note: surface reading: the site of an excellent win over Germany, perhaps a football ground
setter's reading: the cracking is codebreaking, the wartime breaking of German Enigma ciphers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like British slang for excellent, suggesting a sports win; it is literal, the breaking of codes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buckinghamshire estate housed Britain's codebreakers in the Second World War, whose decrypts of German messages helped win the war.

clue.text: Punk singer – he's an eccentric American clad in coat and dress

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters before it are set out in a strange new order
something clad in clothing is wrapped inside it, so one piece goes within the dress

blocks.note: the letters of these two words rearranged
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
a gown is a dress
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A punk frontman is described as an odd American wearing a coat and a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The A sits inside the dress, between its third and fourth letters, after the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shane MacGowan fronted the Pogues, the London Irish band that grew out of the punk scene.

clue.text: Bernstein possibly fat, eating a very long time

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: lard is pig fat
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Someone surmises Bernstein grew fat from eating for an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein, the American composer of West Side Story, is one example of a person with this first name.

clue.text: Unoriginal classical sextet entertained by Guns N' Roses guitarist

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within the host's house, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: Slash is the top-hatted lead guitarist of Guns N' Roses
VI is six in Roman numerals, the classical way of writing it

explanation.surface: A rock guitarist hosts a classical six-piece ensemble, playing derivative music.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish copying follows a model too closely, showing no originality of its own.

clue.text: Time that chap joins band leader once

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
he is the pronoun for that chap
Queen is the rock band of Freddie Mercury

explanation.surface: A man is finally ready to join the group that he once led.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band leader' reads as one phrase, but the band is part of the wordplay and the definition starts at 'leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: The late Elizabeth II, monarch and head of state until 2022, was a national leader in the past.

clue.text: Navigator's wild hounds

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An explorer's pack of dogs has run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Hudson was the English explorer who sailed in search of a northern passage, giving his name to a river and a bay.

clue.text: By church, the setter attempts to conserve energy in resting places

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it safe within, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
the setter refers to themself as me
tries are attempts
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A crossword setter near a church tries to save energy while finding somewhere to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cemeteries are burial grounds, where the dead are said to lie at rest.

clue.text: Blast! English dullard makes a bloomer

blocks.note: both are exclamations of annoyance
E is the abbreviation for English
a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: Someone curses as a dull Englishman makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, which the surface leans on; here it is literally a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The hellebore, such as the Christmas rose, is a flowering plant, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Ancestral ground in English city

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are reformed in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family's ancestral land lies in a city in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the noun land; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is the historic county town of Lancashire in north-west England.

clue.text: Ray Bradbury edited awful manuscript, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Ray Bradbury revised a dreadful draft of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray Bradbury' reads as the science-fiction author's name, but Ray stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is a ray, a shaft of light.

clue.text: Italian smoker's name included in letter from abroad

indicators.note: something included in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An Italian who smokes has his name in a letter from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, which smokes and erupts, so a volcano is jokingly a smoker.

clue.text: Frisky European gent with rice crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lively continental gentleman is served rice crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rice crackers' looks like a snack; crackers is the anagram signal acting on gent and rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means lively and playful, full of energy.

clue.text: Victorian librettist's awful bilge and vacuous rot

indicators.note: awful means very bad, so the word that follows is mangled into another order
vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides and only its outer letters remain

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters of rot

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a Victorian lyricist's words as dreadful nonsense and empty drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for Sullivan's comic operas in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Pass on very soft starter of escalope or port

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
first letter of escalope

explanation.surface: A diner declines a very tender escalope starter, or a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' reads as declining a dish; 'port' looks like the drink but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a ferry port on the Normandy coast of northern France.

clue.text: Calm old man pocketing 50 coppers

indicators.note: pocketing something puts it away inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: A composed elderly man pockets fifty pence in copper coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers looks like small change but means police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means peaceful and not easily upset, the same as calm.

clue.text: Rich Telegraph compilers are going to fuss

blocks.note: the setters speaking of themselves would say 'we'll', meaning we will
taken as written
a to-do is a fuss; the second piece completes it

explanation.surface: The newspaper's wealthy setters intend to kick up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are going to' is rendered by the setters' own contraction we'll, then 'to-do' is a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means prosperous, comfortably off, so it is a synonym for rich.

clue.text: Eighties band with moment to make a comeback in US city

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'
a-ha were the Norwegian pop band behind 'Take On Me'

explanation.surface: A 1980s pop group takes a moment to stage a comeback in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, in the United States.

clue.text: Time for landing cod and manta ray? Only the tails are visible

indicators.note: tails are the hindmost parts, so just the final letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: last letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A cod and a manta ray come ashore with only their tails showing above the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing scene hides the wartime meaning of 'landing'.
explanation.definitionFit: D-Day, 6 June 1944, was the date of the Allied landings in Normandy.

clue.text: Left-winger, entertaining sort, wrote again

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them within the home, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a sort is a type

explanation.surface: A socialist who is fun company has redrafted something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining sort' looks like a description of the left-winger; entertaining is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to type out again, one way to write something a second time.

clue.text: Some like bananas or floral arrangement

indicators.note: some of something is just a part of it, so the letters lie inside the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of like into bananas

explanation.surface: Some people like a bowl of bananas or a vase of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of arranging flowers.

clue.text: Thin ruminant going around yard

indicators.note: going around means turning about to face the other way, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a deer chews the cud, so it is a ruminant
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A skinny cud-chewing animal wanders around a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going around yard' suggests a container round the Y; going around only turns the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice or sound is thin and high, like a reed instrument.

clue.text: Vehicle's reversing around outskirts of Anderlecht … using this for directions?

indicators.note: reversing sends a vehicle backwards, so its letters run in the opposite direction
the outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the first and last letters are kept
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps about the other

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle, and 's adds the S
first and last letters of Anderlecht

explanation.surface: A van backs out around the suburbs of a Brussels district, relying on a gadget for the route.
explanation.walkthrough: Anderlecht is a district of Brussels; only its edges are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav is a satellite navigation device that gives a driver turn-by-turn directions.
